phrases.hindi: तुम्हारा नाम क्या है? (Tumhara naam kya hai?)
तुम कहाँ जा रहे हो? (Tum kahan ja rahe ho?)
क्या तुमने खाना खा लिया? (Kya tumne khana kha liya?)
हाँ, मैंने खा लिया। (Haan, mainne kha liya.)

phrases.english: See you later. / Let's meet later.
phrases.hindi: बाद में मिलते हैं। (Baad mein milte hain.)
तुम क्या कर रहे हो? (Tum kya kar rahe ho?)
क्या तुम्हें पता है? (Kya tumhein pata hai?)

phrases.tamil: உன் வீடு எங்கே இருக்கு? (Un veedu enge irukku?)
phrases.hindi: तुम्हारा घर कहाँ है? (Tumhara ghar kahan hai?)
phrases.telugu: నీ ఇల్లు ఎక్కడ ఉంది? (Nee illu ekkada undi?)

phrases.hindi: यह मेरी माँ है। (Yah meri maa hai.)
यह मेरे पिता हैं। (Yah mere pita hain.)
अच्छे से हंसो / मुस्कुराओ। (Achchhe se hanso / muskurao.)
समय क्या हुआ है? (Samay kya hua hai?)
क्या तुम आज आ रहे हो? (Kya tum aaj aa rahe ho?)
phrases.telugu: నువ్వు ఈ రోజు వస్తున్నావా? (Nuvvu ee roju vastunnavaa?)

phrases.hindi: मैं कल आया था। (Main kal aaya tha.)
बारिश हो रही है। (Baarish ho rahi hai.)
मुझे भूख लग रही है। (Mujhe bhookh lag rahi hai.)
खाने के लिए क्या है? (Khane ke liye kya hai?)
मेरे पेट में दर्द हो रहा है। (Mere pet mein dard ho raha hai.)
phrases.telugu: నా కడుపు నొప్పుగా ఉంది. (Naa kadupu noppuga undi.)

phrases.english: Are you sick? (Is your health not right?)
phrases.hindi: क्या तुम्हारी तबीयत खराब है? (Kya tumhari tabiyat kharab hai?)
मुझे नींद आ रही है। (Mujhe neend aa rahi hai.)

phrases.tamil: நீ என்ன வேலை செய்கிறாய்? (Nee enna velai seigiraai?)
phrases.hindi: तुम क्या काम कर रहे हो? (Tum kya kaam kar rahe ho?)
phrases.telugu: నువ్వు ఏం పని చేస్తున్నావు? (Nuvvu em pani chestunnavu?)

phrases.english: I am going to the forest.
phrases.hindi: मैं जंगल जा रहा हूँ। (Main jangal ja raha hoon.)
काम खत्म हो गया। (Kaam khatam ho gaya.)

phrases.english: There is an animal in the forest.
phrases.hindi: जंगल में जानवर है। (Jangal mein jaanwar hai.)
यह बहुत मुश्किल है। (Yah bahut mushkil hai.)
अच्छे से काम करो। (Achchhe se kaam karo.)

phrases.tamil: நீ ஏன் கோபமா இருக்கிறாய்? (Nee aen kobamaa irukkiraai?)
phrases.hindi: तुम क्यों गुस्सा हो? (Tum kyon gussa ho?)
phrases.telugu: నువ్వు ఎందుకు కోపంగా ఉన్నావు? (Nuvvu enduku kopanga unnavu?)

phrases.hindi: मुझे यह पसंद है। (Mujhe yah pasand hai.)
मुझे यह पसंद नहीं है। (Mujhe yah pasand nahi hai.)
phrases.telugu: నాకు ఇది ఇష్టం లేదు. (Naaku idi ishtam ledu.)

phrases.hindi: यह कितने का है? (Yah kitne ka hai?)
मेरे पास पैसे नहीं हैं। (Mere paas paise nahi hain.)
phrases.telugu: నా దగ్గర డబ్బు లేదు. (Naa daggara dabbu ledu.)

phrases.english: This is too much / a lot.
phrases.hindi: यह बहुत ज़्यादा है। (Yah bahut zyada hai.)
क्या तुम्हारे पास छुट्टे (खुले पैसे) हैं? (Kya tumhare paas chhutte hain?)
phrases.telugu: నీ దగ్గర చిల్లర ఉందా? (Nee daggara chillara unda?)

phrases.tamil: அதை இங்கே கொண்டு வா. (Athai inge kondu vaa.)

phrases.hindi: खून आ रहा है। (Khoon aa raha hai.)
मुझे रास्ता नहीं पता। (Mujhe rasta nahi pata.)
बहुत खुशी हुई / धन्यवाद। (Bahut khushi hui / Dhanyawad.)
मुझे माफ़ कर दो। (Mujhe maaf kar do.)
तुम क्या कह रहे हो? (Tum kya kah rahe ho?)

phrases.english: I am taking leave (I will go and come back).

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Pāmbu kadicha valumbu enga kailu irukku. Ānā, anda kayi dān āyiram usire kāppāttudu. Valiyum oru nāl marundāgum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: The scars of snake bites are on our hands. But those same hands save a thousand lives. One day, even pain becomes medicine.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: பாம்பு கடித்த தழும்பு எங்கள் கையில் உள்ளது. ஆனால், அந்த கை தான் ஆயிரம் உயிரை காப்பாற்றுகிறது. வலியும் ஒரு நாள் மருந்தாகும். (Paambu kaditha thazhumbu engal kaiyil ullathu. Aanaal, antha kai thaan aayiram uyirai kaappaatrugirathu. Valiyum oru naal marunthaagum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: सांप के काटने के निशान हमारे हाथों पर हैं। लेकिन यही हाथ हज़ार जान बचाते हैं। एक दिन दर्द भी दवा बन जाता है। (Saanp ke kaatne ke nishaan hamare hathon par hain. Lekin yahi haath hazar jaan bachate hain. Ek din dard bhi dawa ban jata hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: పాము కాటు గాయాలు మా చేతులపై ఉన్నాయి. కానీ ఆ చేతులే వెయ్యి ప్రాణాలను కాపాడుతాయి. ఒక రోజు నొప్పే మందుగా మారుతుంది. (Paamu kaatu gaayaalu maa chetulapai unnayi. Kaani aa chetule veyyi praanalanu kaapadutayi. Oka roju noppe manduga marutundi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: The Irulas are famous for catching venomous snakes to create antivenom. This story tells the user that their struggles and scars can be the very thing that helps others.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Pulla pasiyilu aludā, tayikku kudukka onnum ille. Appo, oru kuruvi mēlirundu oru palam pōttudu. Iruttu vēleyilum velicham varum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: When the child cried in hunger, the mother had nothing to give. Just then, a little bird dropped a fruit from above. Even in the darkest time, light will come.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: பிள்ளை பசியில் அழுதா, தாய்க்கு கொடுக்க ஒன்னும் இல்ல. அப்போ, ஒரு குருவி மேலிருந்து ஒரு பழம் போட்டது. இருட்டு வேளையிலும் வெளிச்சம் வரும். (Pillai pasiyil azhuthaa, thaaikku kodukka onnum illa. Appo, oru kuruvi maelirunthu oru pazham pottathu. Iruttu velaiyilum velicham varum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: जब बच्चा भूख से रोया, तो माँ के पास देने को कुछ नहीं था। तभी, एक चिड़िया ने ऊपर से एक फल गिरा दिया। अंधेरे समय में भी रोशनी आती है। (Jab bachcha bhookh se roya, toh maa ke paas dene ko kuch nahi tha. Tabhi, ek chidiya ne upar se ek phal gira diya. Andhere samay mein bhi roshni aati hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: పిల్లవాడు ఆకలితో ఏడ్చినప్పుడు, తల్లి దగ్గర ఇవ్వడానికి ఏమీ లేదు. అప్పుడే, ఒక చిన్న పక్షి పైనుండి ఒక పండు కింద పడేసింది. చీకటి సమయంలో కూడా వెలుగు వస్తుంది. (Pillavadu aakalito edchinappudu, talli daggara ivvadaniki emi ledu. Appude, oka chinna pakshi painundi oka pandu kinda padesindi. Cheekati samayamlo kuda velugu vastundi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: A deeply emotional story reflecting the poverty many indigenous communities face, while teaching a motivating lesson to never lose hope when things seem impossible.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Namma mannu vīdu idiñjālum, namma mūdādaiyar pātta yārum alikka mudiyādu. Vēr ālattā irundā, maram tirumbavum valarum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: Even if our mud houses fall, no one can erase the songs of our ancestors. If the roots are deep, the tree will grow again.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: நம்ம மண் வீடு இடிஞ்சாலும், நம்ம மூதாதையர் பாட்டை யாரும் அழிக்க முடியாது. வேர் ஆழமா இருந்தா, மரம் திரும்பவும் வளரும். (Namma man veedu idinjaalum, namma moodhaathaiyar paattai yaarum azhikka mudiyaathu. Vaer aazhama irunthaa, maram thirumbavum valarum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: भले ही हमारे मिट्टी के घर गिर जाएं, लेकिन हमारे पूर्वजों के गीत को कोई नहीं मिटा सकता। अगर जड़ें गहरी हों, तो पेड़ फिर से उगेगा। (Bhale hi hamare mitti ke ghar gir jayein, lekin hamare purvajon ke geet ko koi nahi mita sakta. Agar jadein gahri hon, toh ped phir se ugega.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: మన మట్టి ఇళ్లు కూలిపోయినా, మన పూర్వీకుల పాటను ఎవరూ చెరిపేయలేరు. మూలాలు లోతుగా ఉంటే, చెట్టు మళ్లీ పెరుగుతుంది. (Mana matti illu kulipoyina, mana poorvikula paatanu evaru cherepeiyaleru. Moolalu lotuga unte, chettu malli perugutundi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Many Irulas have lost their native forest lands to modernization. This story evokes sympathy for their loss, but motivates the listener by emphasizing that true identity and strength come from deep cultural roots.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Pasiyōda irunda vēttaikkāran oru kutti māna pāttān. Ade kollāme tayi pōla valattān. Usire edukkardu vīramille, usire kāppāttardu dān nijamāna balam.
stories_or_proverbs.english: The hungry hunter saw a baby deer. Without killing it, he raised it like a mother. Taking a life is not bravery; saving a life is true strength.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: பசியோடு இருந்த வேட்டைக்காரன் ஒரு குட்டி மானை பார்த்தான். அதை கொல்லாமல் தாய் போல வளர்த்தான். உயிரை எடுப்பது வீரமல்ல, உயிரை காப்பாற்றுவதே உண்மையான பலம். (Pasiyodu iruntha vettaikkaaran oru kutti maanai paarthaan. Athai kollaamal thaai pola valarthaan. Uyirai eduppathu veeramalla, uyirai kaappaatruvathey unmaiyaana balam.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: भूखे शिकारी ने एक हिरण के बच्चे को देखा। उसे मारे बिना, उसने उसे एक माँ की तरह पाला। जान लेना वीरता नहीं है; जान बचाना ही सच्ची ताकत है। (Bhookhe shikari ne ek hiran ke bachche ko dekha. Use maare bina, usne use ek maa ki tarah paala. Jaan lena veerta nahi hai; jaan bachana hi sachchi taqat hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: ఆకలితో ఉన్న వేటగాడు ఒక జింక పిల్లను చూశాడు. దానిని చంపకుండా, తల్లిలా పెంచాడు. ప్రాణం తీయడం వీరత్వం కాదు, ప్రాణం నిలపడమే నిజమైన బలం. (Aakalito unna vetagadu oka jinka pillanu chusadu. Danini champakunda, tallila penchadu. Pranam tiyadam veeratvam kadu, pranam nilapadame nijamaina balam.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: A touching narrative showing that despite being historically hunter-gatherers, the Irulas possess profound empathy and respect for forest life.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Veyyilu mēle pattālum, pulla padikkanunnu seruppu illāme nadandān. Viyarve sotta sotta ulachā, oru nāl anda pulla avane nelalukku kūttitu pōvān.
stories_or_proverbs.english: Even though the sun burned him, he walked without shoes so his child could study. If you sweat and work hard, one day that child will take you to the shade.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: வெயில் மேலே பட்டாலும், பிள்ளை படிக்கணுன்னு செருப்பு இல்லாம நடந்தான். வியர்வை சொட்ட சொட்ட உழைச்சா, ஒரு நாள் அந்த பிள்ளை அவனை நிழலுக்கு கூட்டிட்டு போவான். (Veyil maele pattaalum, pillai padikkanunnu seruppu illaama nadanthaan. Viyarvai sotta sotta uzhaichaa, oru naal antha pillai avanai nizhalukku koottittu povaan.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: धूप जलने पर भी, वह बिना चप्पल के चला ताकि उसका बच्चा पढ़ सके। पसीना बहाकर मेहनत करोगे, तो एक दिन वही बच्चा तुम्हें छांव में ले जाएगा। (Dhoop jalne par bhi, vah bina chappal ke chala taaki uska bachcha padh sake. Paseena bahakar mehnat karoge, toh ek din wahi bachcha tumhein chhanv mein le jayega.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: ఎండ మండుతున్నా, తన బిడ్డ చదువుకోవాలని చెప్పులు లేకుండా నడిచాడు. చెమటోడ్చి కష్టపడితే, ఒక రోజు ఆ బిడ్డే అతన్ని నీడకు తీసుకెళ్తాడు. (Enda mandutunna, tana bidda chaduvukovalani cheppulu lekunda nadichadu. Chematodchi kashtapadite, oka roju aa bidde atanni needaku teesukeltadu.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Many Irula families transition into hard labor like brick kilns after losing forest access. This story brings sympathy to their struggle while motivating with the hope of education.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Tanni vēgamā ōdina, ottaiyā pōgumpōdu vellam adichu pōidum. Ānā, nālu pēr kai pidiñjā, anda vellamē oru pālamāgīdum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: If the river runs fast, going alone means the flood will wash you away. But if four people hold hands, that very flood becomes a bridge.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: தண்ணீர் வேகமா ஓடினா, ஒத்தையா போகும்போது வெள்ளம் அடிச்சு போயிடும். ஆனா, நாலு பேர் கை பிடிஞ்சா, அந்த வெள்ளமே ஒரு பாலமாகிடும். (Thanneer vegamaa odinaa, othaiyaa pogumbothu vellam adichu poyidum. Aanaa, naalu per kai pidinjaa, antha vellame oru paalamaagidum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: अगर पानी तेज़ बहता है, तो अकेले जाने पर बाढ़ तुम्हें बहा ले जाएगी। लेकिन अगर चार लोग हाथ पकड़ लें, तो वही बाढ़ एक पुल बन जाती है। (Agar paani tez bahta hai, toh akele jaane par baadh tumhein baha le jayegi. Lekin agar chaar log haath pakad lein, toh wahi baadh ek pul ban jaati hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: నీరు వేగంగా పారుతున్నప్పుడు, ఒంటరిగా వెళితే వరద నిన్ను కొట్టుకుపోయేలా చేస్తుంది. కానీ నలుగురు చేతులు పట్టుకుంటే, ఆ వరద కూడా వంతెన అవుతుంది. (Neeru veganga parutunnappudu, ontariga velite varada ninnu kottukupoyela chestundi. Kaani naluguru chetulu pattukunte, aa varada kuda vantena avutundi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: A powerful metaphor for tribal unity. It teaches users that facing life's biggest obstacles is impossible alone, but togetherness turns the obstacle itself into a path.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Iruttulu pūtta pūvu, yārukkum teriyādu. Ānā adoda vāsane kāttu pūra nirañjirukku. Namma uleppu veliye teriyāttālum, namma manasu suttama irukku.
stories_or_proverbs.english: The flower that bloomed in the dark is known to no one. But its fragrance fills the entire forest. Even if our hard work is not seen by the outside world, our hearts remain pure.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: இருட்டில் பூத்த பூ, யாருக்கும் தெரியாது. ஆனால் அதோட வாசனை காடு பூரா நிறைஞ்சிருக்கு. நம்ம உழைப்பு வெளியே தெரியாட்டாலும், நம்ம மனசு சுத்தமா இருக்கு. (Iruttil pootha poo, yaarukkum theriyaathu. Aanaal athoda vaasanai kaadu poora niranjirukku. Namma uzhaippu veliye theriyaattaalum, namma manasu suthamaa irukku.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: अंधेरे में खिले फूल को कोई नहीं जानता। लेकिन उसकी खुशबू पूरे जंगल में भरी होती है। भले ही हमारी मेहनत बाहर न दिखे, लेकिन हमारा दिल साफ है। (Andhere mein khile phool ko koi nahi jaanta. Lekin uski khushboo poore jangal mein bhari hoti hai. Bhale hi hamari mehnat bahar na dikhe, lekin hamara dil saaf hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: చీకటిలో వికసించిన పువ్వు ఎవరికీ తెలియదు. కానీ దాని సువాసన అడవి అంతా నిండి ఉంటుంది. మన కష్టం బయటకు కనిపించకపోయినా, మన మనస్సు స్వచ్ఛంగా ఉంటుంది. (Chikatilo vikasinchina puvvu evariki teliyadu. Kaani daani suvasana adavi antaa nindi untundi. Mana kashtam bayataku kanipinchakapoyina, mana manassu svacchanga untundi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: A poetic reflection on the unseen struggles of the Irula people. It motivates the user to keep doing good and working hard, even if they aren't receiving recognition from society.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Rendu pērukku ore oru kelañgu dān irundadu. Pasiyilum ade pādi pādiyā piriñju tinna pōdu, adu rājavā vālra mādiri ānandam tandadu. Kudukkarda dān unmaiyāna vālkke.
stories_or_proverbs.english: Two people had only one wild tuber. Even in deep hunger, when they split it in half and ate, it gave them the joy of living like kings. Giving is the true way of life.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: ரெண்டு பேருக்கு ஒரே ஒரு கிழங்கு தான் இருந்தது. பசியிலும் அதை பாதி பாதியா பிரிஞ்சு தின்ன போது, அது ராஜாவா வாழ்ற மாதிரி ஆனந்தம் தந்தது. கொடுக்கறது தான் உண்மையான வாழ்க்கை. (Rendu perukku ore oru kizhangu thaan irunthathu. Pasiyilum athai paathi paathiyaa pirinju thinna pothu, athu raajavaa vaazhra maathiri aanantham thanthathu. Kodukkarathu thaan unmaiyaana vaazhkkai.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: दो लोगों के पास सिर्फ एक कंद (शकरकंद) था। गहरी भूख में भी जब उन्होंने उसे आधा-आधा बांटकर खाया, तो उसने राजा की तरह जीने का आनंद दिया। देना ही सच्चा जीवन है। (Do logon ke paas sirf ek kand tha. Gahri bhookh mein bhi jab unhone use aadha-aadha baantkar khaya, toh usne raja ki tarah jeene ka anand diya. Dena hi sachcha jeevan hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: ఇద్దరు మనుషులకు ఒకే ఒక్క దుంప ఉంది. తీవ్రమైన ఆకలిలో కూడా దానిని సగం సగం పంచుకుని తిన్నప్పుడు, అది రాజులా బతికిన ఆనందాన్ని ఇచ్చింది. ఇవ్వడమే నిజమైన జీవితం. (Iddaru manushulaku oke okka dumpa undi. Tivramaina aakalilo kuda daanini sagam sagam panchukuni tinnappudu, adi rajula batikina anandanni icchindi. Ivvadame nijamaina jivitam.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Historically, Irulas relied heavily on forest tubers (kelangu) for survival. This story touches the heart by showing that true wealth lies in sharing whatever little you have, even during starvation.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Tāttā pōgum pōdu, oru kādē alinda mādiri irundadu. Pustagattulu illāda arivu, avanga padutta pāyilu dān irukku. Namma periyavange madippadu dān namma unmaiyāna sottu.
stories_or_proverbs.english: When the old grandfather passed away, it felt like an entire forest was destroyed. The knowledge not found in books was left on the mat where he slept. Respecting our elders is our true wealth.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: தாத்தா போகும் போது, ஒரு காடே அழிந்த மாதிரி இருந்தது. புத்தகத்தில் இல்லாத அறிவு, அவங்க படுத்த பாயில் தான் இருக்கு. நம்ம பெரியவங்களை மதிப்பதே நம்ம உண்மையான சொத்து. (Thaathaa pogum pothu, oru kaade azhintha maathiri irunthathu. Puthagathil illaatha arivu, avanga padutha paayil thaan irukku. Namma periyavangalai mathippathe namma unmaiyaana sothu.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: जब बूढ़े दादा का निधन हुआ, तो लगा जैसे पूरा जंगल उजड़ गया। किताबों में न मिलने वाला ज्ञान उनकी चटाई पर ही रह गया। अपने बड़ों का सम्मान करना ही हमारी असली संपत्ति है। (Jab boodhe dada ka nidhan hua, toh laga jaise poora jangal ujad gaya. Kitabon mein na milne wala gyaan unki chatai par hi rah gaya. Apne badon ka samman karna hi hamari asli sampatti hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: తాత చనిపోయినప్పుడు, ఒక అడవే నాశనమైనట్లు అనిపించింది. పుస్తకాలలో దొరకని జ్ఞానం వారు పడుకున్న చాప మీదే ఉండిపోయింది. మన పెద్దలను గౌరవించడమే మన నిజమైన సంపద. (Taata chanipoyinappudu, oka adave nashanamainatlu anipinchindi. Pustakalalo dorakani gnanam vaaru padukunna chapa meede undipoyindi. Mana peddalanu gouravinchadame mana nijamaina sampada.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Since the Irula language has no traditional script, all their deep knowledge of nature, medicine, and survival is passed down orally. This story motivates the youth to cherish the elderly before their wisdom is lost forever.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Yāne namma kūreye idicha nālu, nāmbu kōvappattōm. Ānā, kādulu pākkum pōdu ade pullakku kodukka onnum ille. Pasi ellārukkum onnu dān. Yār mannu yārukku sondam?
stories_or_proverbs.english: The day the elephant destroyed our hut, we got angry. But when we looked into the forest, it had nothing to give to its calf. Hunger is the same for everyone. Whose land belongs to whom?
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: யானை நம்ம கூரையை இடித்த நாள், நாம் கோபப்பட்டோம். ஆனால், காட்டில் பார்க்கும் போது அதோட பிள்ளைக்கு கொடுக்க ஒன்னும் இல்ல. பசி எல்லாருக்கும் ஒன்னு தான். யார் மண் யாருக்கு சொந்தம்? (Yaanai namma kooraiyai iditha naal, naam kovappattom. Aanaal, kaattil paarkkum pothu athoda pillaikku kodukka onnum illa. Pasi ellaarukkum onnu thaan. Yaar man yaarukku sontham?)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: जिस दिन हाथी ने हमारी झोपड़ी तोड़ी, हमें बहुत गुस्सा आया। लेकिन जंगल में देखने पर, उसके पास अपने बच्चे को देने के लिए कुछ नहीं था। भूख सबके लिए एक है। किसकी ज़मीन किसकी है? (Jis din hathi ne hamari jhopdi todi, hamein bahut gussa aaya. Lekin jangal mein dekhne par, uske paas apne bachche ko dene ke liye kuch nahi tha. Bhookh sabke liye ek hai. Kiski zameen kiski hai?)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: ఏనుగు మన గుడిసెను పడగొట్టిన రోజు మనం కోపపడ్డాము. కానీ అడవిలో చూసినప్పుడు, దాని బిడ్డకు ఇవ్వడానికి ఏమీ లేదు. ఆకలి అందరికీ ఒక్కటే. ఎవరి భూమి ఎవరికి సొంతం? (Aenugu mana gudisenu padagottina roju manam kopapaddamu. Kaani adavilo chusinappudu, daani biddaku ivvadaniki emi ledu. Aakali andariki okkate. Evari bhumi evariki sontam?)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Irulas live on the fringes of forests and frequently face human-wildlife conflicts. This story beautifully illustrates their immense empathy, showing that even when they lose their homes, they understand the pain of the animals whose forests have been destroyed.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Mūngil kūde pinnum pōdu, tayoda kayil rattam vandadu. Ānā anda kūdeyil dān pullakku sāppādu nirañjirukkum. Valige ellām nālekku vālkke āgum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: When weaving the bamboo basket, blood came from the mother's hands. But it is in that basket the child's food will be filled. All pain becomes tomorrow's life.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: மூங்கில் கூடை பின்னும் போது, தாயின் கையில் ரத்தம் வந்தது. ஆனா அந்த கூடையில் தான் பிள்ளைக்கு சாப்பாடு நிறைஞ்சிருக்கும். வலிகள் எல்லாம் நாளைக்கு வாழ்க்கையாகும். (Moongil koodai pinnum pothu, thaayin kaiyil ratham vanthathu. Aanaa antha koodaiyil thaan pillaikku saappaadu niranjirukkum. Valigal ellaam naalaikku vaazhkkaiyaagum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: बांस की टोकरी बुनते समय, माँ के हाथ से खून निकल आया। लेकिन उसी टोकरी में बच्चे का खाना भरा जाएगा। सारा दर्द कल का जीवन बन जाता है। (Baans ki tokari bunte samay, maa ke haath se khoon nikal aaya. Lekin usi tokari mein bachche ka khana bhara jayega. Saara dard kal ka jeevan ban jaata hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: వెదురు బుట్ట అల్లుతున్నప్పుడు, తల్లి చేతి నుండి రక్తం వచ్చింది. కానీ ఆ బుట్టలోనే బిడ్డకు అన్నం నిండుతుంది. నొప్పులన్నీ రేపటి జీవితంగా మారుతాయి. (Veduru butta allutunnappudu, talli cheti nundi raktam vachindi. Kaani aa buttalone biddaku annam nindutundi. Noppulanni repati jeevitanga marutayi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Irula women are highly skilled artisans who make cane and bamboo products. This story brings sympathy to their hard labor while motivating the youth to remember their parents' sacrifices.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Kōde kālatulu, kādu pūra kāñjupōchu. Kidaicha oru vayā tanniye, periyavar oru dāgam ulla nāykku kuduttār. Punniyam dān namma usire kāppāttum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: In the summer time, the whole forest dried up. The old man gave the one cup of water he found to a thirsty dog. It is good deeds alone that protect our lives.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: கோடை காலத்துல, காடு பூரா காஞ்சுபோச்சு. கிடைச்ச ஒரு வாய் தண்ணியை, பெரியவர் ஒரு தாகம் உள்ள நாய்க்கு கொடுத்தார். புண்ணியம் தான் நம்ம உயிரை காப்பாற்றும். (Kodai kaalathula, kaadu poora kaanjupochu. Kidaicha oru vaai thanniyai, periyavar oru thaagam ulla naaikku koduthaar. Punniyam thaan namma uyirai kaappaatrum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: गर्मियों के मौसम में पूरा जंगल सूख गया। बूढ़े आदमी ने उसे मिला एक घूंट पानी एक प्यासे कुत्ते को दे दिया। केवल अच्छे कर्म ही हमारी जान बचाते हैं। (Garmiyon ke mausam mein poora jangal sookh gaya. Boodhe aadmi ne use mila ek ghoont paani ek pyaase kutte ko de diya. Keval achchhe karm hi hamari jaan bachate hain.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: వేసవి కాలంలో అడవి అంతా ఎండిపోయింది. వృద్ధుడు తనకు దొరికిన ఒక్క గుక్క నీటిని దాహంతో ఉన్న కుక్కకు ఇచ్చాడు. పుణ్యమే మన ప్రాణాలను కాపాడుతుంది. (Vesavi kaalamlo adavi antaa endipoyindi. Vruddhudu tanaku dorikina okka gukka neetini dahamto unna kukkaku icchadu. Punyame mana pranalanu kapadutundi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Droughts severely impact marginalized tribal settlements. This touching story illustrates the deep indigenous ethos of sharing Earth's scarce resources with all creatures, even before oneself.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Pulla vellāduttukku bomme ille, mannu dān irundadu. Ānā anda mannilu kattina vīdu, rāja kōtteye vida alagā irundadu. Santhōsam sothulu ille, manasulu irukku.
stories_or_proverbs.english: The child had no toys to play with, only mud. But the house built in that mud was more beautiful than a king's fort. Happiness is not in wealth, it is in the heart.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: பிள்ளை விளையாட பொம்மை இல்லை, மண் தான் இருந்தது. ஆனா அந்த மண்ணில் கட்டின வீடு, ராஜா கோட்டையை விட அழகா இருந்தது. சந்தோஷம் சொத்தில் இல்லை, மனசில் இருக்கு. (Pillai vilaiyaada bommai illai, man thaan irunthathu. Aanaa antha mannil kattina veedu, raaja kottaiyai vida azhagaa irunthathu. Santhosham sothil illai, manasil irukku.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: बच्चे के खेलने के लिए खिलौने नहीं थे, सिर्फ मिट्टी थी। लेकिन उस मिट्टी में बना घर राजा के महल से भी सुंदर था। खुशी संपत्ति में नहीं, दिल में है। (Bachche ke khelne ke liye khilaune nahi the, sirf mitti thi. Lekin us mitti mein bana ghar raja ke mahal se bhi sundar tha. Khushi sampatti mein nahi, dil mein hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: పిల్లవాడికి ఆడుకోవడానికి బొమ్మలు లేవు, మట్టి మాత్రమే ఉంది. కానీ ఆ మట్టిలో కట్టిన ఇల్లు రాజు కోట కంటే అందంగా ఉంది. సంతోషం ఆస్తిలో లేదు, మనసులో ఉంది. (Pillavadiki aadukovadaniki bommalu levu, matti matrame undi. Kaani aa mattilo kattina illu raaju kota kante andanga undi. Santhosham aastilo ledu, manasulo undi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: A touching observation of tribal children who grow up in extreme poverty but maintain a pure, unbreakable spirit. It motivates the user to appreciate the simple things in life.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Avane kēli panniyavanukku nōyu vandapōdu, pacha ele marundu kuduttu kāppāttinān. Pagaivanukkum uyir onnu dān. Marundu vali tīrkkum, mannippu manase tīrkkum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: When the one who mocked him fell ill, he saved him by giving him green leaf medicine. Even an enemy has only one life. Medicine cures the pain, forgiveness cures the heart.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: அவனை கேலி பண்ணியவனுக்கு நோய் வந்தபோது, பச்சை இலை மருந்து கொடுத்து காப்பாற்றினான். பகைவனுக்கும் உயிர் ஒன்னு தான். மருந்து வலியை தீர்க்கும், மன்னிப்பு மனசை தீர்க்கும். (Avanai keli panniyavanukku noyu vanthapothu, pachai ilai marunthu koduthu kaappaatrinaan. Pagaivanukkum uyir onnu thaan. Marunthu valiyai theerkkum, mannippu manasai theerkkum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: जब उसका मज़ाक उड़ाने वाला बीमार पड़ा, तो उसने हरी पत्ती की दवा देकर उसे बचाया। दुश्मन की भी एक ही जान होती है। दवा दर्द दूर करती है, माफ़ी दिल को ठीक करती है। (Jab uska mazaak udaane wala beemar pada, toh usne hari patti ki dawa dekar use bachaya. Dushman ki bhi ek hi jaan hoti hai. Dawa dard door karti hai, maafi dil ko theek karti hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: అతన్ని ఎగతాళి చేసినవాడు అనారోగ్యానికి గురైనప్పుడు, పచ్చని ఆకు మందు ఇచ్చి కాపాడాడు. శత్రువుకు కూడా ప్రాణం ఒక్కటే. మందు నొప్పిని తగ్గిస్తుంది, క్షమాపణ మనసును బాగుచేస్తుంది. (Atanni egatali chesinavadu anarogyaliki gurainappudu, pachani aaku mandu icchi kapadadu. Satruvuku kuda pranam okkate. Mandu noppini taggistundi, kshamapana manasunu baguchestundi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Historically, Irulas have been marginalized by mainstream society. This powerful story shows their moral high ground, using their invaluable herbal knowledge to heal even those who treat them poorly.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Iruttulu pasiyōda tūnga pōna pullakku, tayi nilāve kāmichu sōru ūtina. Nambikke dān ēlaiyoda mudal unavu.
stories_or_proverbs.english: To the child going to sleep hungry in the dark, the mother showed the moon and fed him hope. Belief is the first food of the poor.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: இருட்டில் பசியோடு தூங்க போன பிள்ளைக்கு, தாய் நிலாவை காமிச்சு சோறு ஊட்டினா. நம்பிக்கை தான் ஏழையோட முதல் உணவு. (Iruttil pasiyodu thoonga pona pillaikku, thaai nilaavai kaamichu soru oottinaa. Nambikkai thaan ezhaiyoda muthal unavu.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: अंधेरे में भूखे सोने गए बच्चे को, माँ ने चाँद दिखाकर उम्मीद खिलाई। विश्वास ही गरीबों का पहला भोजन है। (Andhere mein bhookhe sone gaye bachche ko, maa ne chaand dikhakar ummeed khilai. Vishwas hi garibon ka pahla bhojan hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: చీకటిలో ఆకలితో పడుకోబోయిన బిడ్డకు, తల్లి చంద్రుడిని చూపించి ఆశను తినిపించింది. నమ్మకమే పేదల మొదటి ఆహారం. (Chikatilo aakalito padukoboyina biddaku, talli chandrudini chupinchi aashanu tinipinchindi. Nammakame pedala modati aaharam.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Extreme poverty is a tragic reality for many tribal families. This heart-touching story shows that even when a mother cannot provide food, her love and the ability to inspire hope give the child the strength to survive.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Kādulu namma kālttadam padiya kūdādu nnu nadandōm. Ānā nādu ābattulu mātikkitta pōdu, namma uleppu dān mudalla ninnudu. Amaidi dān namma āyudam.
stories_or_proverbs.english: We walked so our footprints wouldn't fall in the forest. But when the country was in danger, our hard work stood first. Silence is our weapon.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: காட்டில் நம்ம கால் தடம் பதிய கூடாதுன்னு நடந்தோம். ஆனா நாடு ஆபத்துல மாட்டிக்கிட்ட போது, நம்ம உழைப்பு தான் முதல்ல நின்னுது. அமைதி தான் நம்ம ஆயுதம். (Kaattil namma kaal thadam pathiya koodaathunnu nadanthom. Aanaa naadu aabathula maattikkitta pothu, namma uzhaippu thaan muthalla ninnuthu. Amaithi thaan namma aayutham.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: हम ऐसे चले कि जंगल में हमारे पैरों के निशान न पड़ें। लेकिन जब देश खतरे में पड़ा, तो हमारी मेहनत सबसे आगे खड़ी हुई। खामोशी ही हमारा हथियार है। (Hum aise chale ki jangal mein hamare pairon ke nishaan na padein. Lekin jab desh khatre mein pada, toh hamari mehnat sabse aage khadi hui. Khamoshi hi hamara hathiyar hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: అడవిలో మన పాదముద్రలు పడకూడదని నడిచాము. కానీ దేశం ఆపదలో ఉన్నప్పుడు, మన శ్రమే ముందు నిలబడింది. నిశ్శబ్దమే మన ఆయుధం. (Adavilo mana paadamudralu padakudadani nadichamu. Kaani desam aapadalo unnappudu, mana shrame mundu nilabadindi. Nishshabdame mana aayudham.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Irulas live sustainably, trying to leave no trace in nature. Yet, when urban areas face dangerous snake encounters, it is the silent, marginalized Irula snake catcher who arrives to save the day.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Marundukku vēra eleye parikkum pōdu periyavar sonnār, 'Ele kīle vilundā mannu, mēle irundā marundu. Manisanum appadi dān.' Anbu dān madippe kūttum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: While picking roots for medicine, the elder said, 'If the leaf falls, it is just dirt; if it is above, it is medicine. Humans are like that too.' It is love that increases our value.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: மருந்துக்கு வேரை இலையை பறிக்கும் போது பெரியவர் சொன்னார், 'இலை கீழே விழுந்தா மண், மேலே இருந்தா மருந்து. மனுஷனும் அப்படி தான்.' அன்பு தான் மதிப்பை கூட்டும். (Marunthukku verai ilaiyai parikkum pothu periyavar sonnaar, 'Ilai keezhe vizhunthaa man, maele irunthaa marunthu. Manushanum appadi thaan.' Anbu thaan mathippai koottum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: दवा के लिए जड़ें और पत्ते तोड़ते समय बुजुर्ग ने कहा, 'पत्ता नीचे गिरे तो मिट्टी, ऊपर रहे तो दवा। इंसान भी ऐसा ही है।' प्यार ही हमारी कीमत बढ़ाता है। (Dawa ke liye jadein aur patte todte samay buzurg ne kaha, 'Patta neeche gire toh mitti, upar rahe toh dawa. Insaan bhi aisa hi hai.' Pyaar hi hamari keemat badhata hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: మందు కోసం వేరు, ఆకు కోస్తున్నప్పుడు పెద్దాయన అన్నాడు, 'ఆకు కింద పడితే మట్టి, పైన ఉంటే మందు. మనిషి కూడా అంతే.' ప్రేమే మన విలువను పెంచుతుంది. (Mandu kosam veru, aaku kostunnappudu peddayana annadu, 'Aaku kinda padite matti, paina unte mandu. Manishikuda ante.' Preme mana viluvanu penchutundi.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: A beautiful philosophical truth shared by an Irula herbalist. It gently reminds the user that a person's worth is defined by how they lift others up, not by their status or wealth.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Periya kattadatte kattina kayilu, pattāsu sudum pōdu rēge illa. Nām kattina vīttukku nāmbu pōga mudiyādu. Ānā namma sirippe yārum pudunga mudiyādu.
stories_or_proverbs.english: The hands that built the big building have no fingerprints left after making firecrackers. We cannot go into the house we built. But no one can steal our smile.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: பெரிய கட்டடத்தை கட்டின கையில், பட்டாசு சுடும் போது ரேகை இல்லை. நாம் கட்டின வீட்டுக்கு நாம் போக முடியாது. ஆனா நம்ம சிரிப்பை யாரும் பிடுங்க முடியாது. (Periya kattadathai kattina kaiyil, pattaasu sudum pothu regai illai. Naam kattina veettukku naambu poga mudiyaathu. Aanaa namma sirippai yaarum pidunga mudiyaathu.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: बड़ी इमारत बनाने वाले हाथों में, पटाखे बनाते समय लकीरें नहीं बचीं। हम अपने ही बनाए घर में नहीं जा सकते। लेकिन हमारी मुस्कान कोई नहीं छीन सकता। (Badi imarat banane wale hathon mein, patakhe banate samay lakirein nahi bachin. Hum apne hi banaye ghar mein nahi ja sakte. Lekin hamari muskaan koi nahi chheen sakta.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: పెద్ద భవనాన్ని కట్టిన చేతుల్లో, టపాకాయలు చేసేటప్పుడు రేఖలు లేవు. మనం కట్టిన ఇంట్లోకి మనం వెళ్ళలేము. కానీ మన చిరునవ్వును ఎవరూ లాక్కోలేరు. (Pedda bhavananni kattina chetullo, tapakayalu chesetappudu rekhalu levu. Manam kattina intloki manam vellalemu. Kaani mana chirunavvunu evaru laakkoleru.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Many marginalized Irula laborers migrate to cities for construction work or dangerous firecracker manufacturing. This story captures the heart-wrenching reality of their labor, offset by their unbreakable spirit and joy.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Pāmbu pidikkum pōdu, periyavar adu kitte mannippu kēttār. 'Nī emme kottale, nāmbu unne kollamāttōm. Oru usire kāppātta innoru usirukku vali kodukka kūdādu.'
stories_or_proverbs.english: When catching the snake, the elder asked it for forgiveness. 'You did not sting us, we will not kill you. To save one life, we should not give pain to another.'
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: பாம்பு பிடிக்கும் போது, பெரியவர் அது கிட்ட மன்னிப்பு கேட்டார். 'நீ எங்களை கொட்டல, நாம உன்னை கொல்லமாட்டோம். ஒரு உயிரை காப்பாற்ற இன்னொரு உயிருக்கு வலி கொடுக்க கூடாது.' (Paambu pidikkum pothu, periyavar athu kitta mannippu kettaar. 'Nee engalai kottala, naama unnai kollamaattom. Oru uyirai kaappaatra innoru uyirukku vali kodukka koodaathu.')
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: सांप को पकड़ते समय, बुजुर्ग ने उससे माफ़ी मांगी। 'तुमने हमें नहीं काटा, हम तुम्हें नहीं मारेंगे। एक जान को बचाने के लिए दूसरी जान को दर्द नहीं देना चाहिए।' (Saanp ko pakadte samay, buzurg ne usse maafi maangi. 'Tumne hamein nahi kaata, hum tumhein nahi maarenge. Ek jaan ko bachane ke liye doosri jaan ko dard nahi dena chahiye.')
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: పామును పట్టుకునేటప్పుడు, పెద్దాయన దానిని క్షమాపణ కోరాడు. 'నువ్వు మమ్మల్ని కాటు వేయలేదు, మేము నిన్ను చంపము. ఒక ప్రాణాన్ని కాపాడటానికి ఇంకో ప్రాణానికి నొప్పి కలిగించకూడదు.' (Paamunu pattukunetappudu, peddayana daanini kshamapana koradu. 'Nuvvu mammalni kaatu veyaledu, memu ninnu champamu. Oka prananni kapadatani inko prananniki noppi kaliginchakudadu.')
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Despite their dangerous profession, Irulas deeply revere snakes. This story evokes sympathy for the misunderstood snake catchers, illustrating their profound ethical code and compassion for all living beings.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Tēne vikkum pōdu yārum vele tarale. Ānā ava sirichā, ēn-na anda tēne edukka ava paṭṭa vali malekku dān teriyum. Namma madippe nāmbu dān unaranum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: When selling honey, no one gave a fair price. But she smiled, because only the mountain knows the pain she endured to get it. We must realize our own worth.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: தேனை விற்கும் போது யாரும் விலை தரலை. ஆனா அவ சிரிச்சா, ஏன்னா அந்த தேனை எடுக்க அவ பட்ட வலி மலைக்கு தான் தெரியும். நம்ம மதிப்பை நாம் தான் உணரணும். (Thaenai virkum pothu yaarum vilai tharalai. Aanaa ava sirichaa, aennaa antha thaenai edukka ava patta vali malaikku thaan theriyum. Namma mathippai naam thaan unaranum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: शहद बेचते समय किसी ने सही कीमत नहीं दी। लेकिन वह मुस्कुराई, क्योंकि उस शहद को निकालने में उसने जो दर्द सहा, वह सिर्फ पहाड़ जानता है। हमें अपनी कीमत खुद पहचाननी चाहिए। (Shahad bechte samay kisi ne sahi keemat nahi di. Lekin vah muskurai, kyonki us shahad ko nikaalne mein usne jo dard saha, vah sirf pahad jaanta hai. Hamein apni keemat khud pahchanni chahiye.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: తేనె అమ్మేటప్పుడు ఎవరూ సరైన ధర ఇవ్వలేదు. కానీ ఆమె నవ్వింది, ఎందుకంటే ఆ తేనె తీయడానికి ఆమె పడిన బాధ పర్వతానికి మాత్రమే తెలుసు. మన విలువను మనమే గుర్తించాలి. (Tene ammetappudu evaru saraina dhara ivvaledu. Kaani aame navvindi, endukante aa tene tiyadaniki aame padina badha parvatanki matrame telusu. Mana viluvanu maname gurtinchali.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: City dwellers often bargain harshly with tribal forest gatherers, not realizing the life-threatening risks taken to collect wild honey. This story motivates the user to never let ignorant people define their value.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Iruttulu padikkum pullakku, tayi minmini pūchiye pudichu velicham kāmichā. Sūriyan illādappo, oru sinna pūchi kūda namma vālkkaiye velichamākkum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: To the child studying in the dark, the mother caught a firefly to give light. When there is no sun, even a small insect can light up our life.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: இருட்டில் படிக்கும் பிள்ளைக்கு, தாய் மின்மினி பூச்சியை பிடித்து வெளிச்சம் காமிச்சா. சூரியன் இல்லாதப்போ, ஒரு சின்ன பூச்சி கூட நம்ம வாழ்க்கையை வெளிச்சமாக்கும். (Iruttil padikkum pillaikku, thaai minmini poochiyai pidithu velicham kaamichaa. Sooriyan illaathappo, oru sinna poochi kooda namma vaazhkkaiyai velichamaakkum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: अंधेरे में पढ़ते बच्चे को, माँ ने जुगनू पकड़कर रोशनी दिखाई। जब सूरज नहीं होता, तो एक छोटा सा कीड़ा भी हमारे जीवन को रोशन कर सकता है। (Andhere mein padhte bachche ko, maa ne jugnu pakadkar roshni dikhai. Jab sooraj nahi hota, toh ek chhota sa keeda bhi hamare jeevan ko roshan kar sakta hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: చీకటిలో చదువుకుంటున్న బిడ్డకు, తల్లి మిణుగురు పురుగును పట్టుకుని వెలుగు చూపించింది. సూర్యుడు లేనప్పుడు, ఒక చిన్న పురుగు కూడా మన జీవితాన్ని కాంతివంతం చేయగలదు. (Cheekatilo chaduvukuntunna biddaku, talli minuguru purugunu pattukuni velugu chupinchindi. Suryudu lenappudu, oka chinna purugu kuda mana jeevitanni kaantivantam cheyagaladu.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Many remote tribal hamlets still lack reliable electricity. This touching story captures a mother's desperate, beautiful love to ensure her child gets an education, showing that even the smallest glimmer of hope can lead to a bright future.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Sengal sūleyilu vēkkaiyilu manneyē pisañjān. Adu vīdu kattumbōdu yārukkum teriyādu, anda mannilu oru ēleyoda viyarveyum kanneerum kalandirukkunnu. Uleppu dān oru manisanoda unmaiyāna adeiyālam.
stories_or_proverbs.english: In the heat of the brick kiln, he kneaded the earth. When it builds a house, no one will know that a poor man's sweat and tears are mixed in that clay. Hard work is a person's true identity.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: செங்கல் சூளையில் வெக்கையில் மண்ணையே பிசைந்தான். அது வீடு கட்டும்போது யாருக்கும் தெரியாது, அந்த மண்ணில் ஒரு ஏழையோட வியர்வையும் கண்ணீரும் கலந்திருக்குன்னு. உழைப்பு தான் ஒரு மனுஷனோட உண்மையான அடையாளம். (Sengal soolaiyil vekkaiyil mannaiyae pisainthaan. Athu veedu kattumbothu yaarukkum theriyaathu, antha mannil oru ezhaiyoda viyarvaiyum kanneerum kalanthirukkunnu. Uzhaippu thaan oru manushanoda unmaiyaana adaiyaalam.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: ईंट भट्ठे की गर्मी में, उसने मिट्टी को गूंथा। जब वह घर बनाएगा, तो किसी को नहीं पता चलेगा कि उस मिट्टी में एक गरीब का पसीना और आंसू मिले हुए हैं। मेहनत ही इंसान की असली पहचान है। (Eent bhatthe ki garmi mein, usne mitti ko goontha. Jab vah ghar banayega, toh kisi ko nahi pata chalega ki us mitti mein ek gareeb ka paseena aur aansu mile hue hain. Mehnat hi insaan ki asli pehchaan hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: ఇటుక బట్టీ వేడిలో, అతను మట్టిని పిసికాడు. అది ఇల్లు కట్టేటప్పుడు ఎవరికీ తెలియదు, ఆ మట్టిలో ఒక పేదవాడి చెమట, కన్నీళ్లు కలిసి ఉన్నాయని. శ్రమే ఒక మనిషి నిజమైన గుర్తింపు. (Ituka battee vedilo, atanu mattini pisikadu. Adi illu kattetappudu evariki teliyadu, aa mattilo oka pedavadi chemata, kanneellu kalisi unnayani. Shrame oka manishi nijamaina gurtimpu.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: Generations of displaced tribal people work as laborers in brick kilns. This story brings visibility and deep sympathy to their unseen struggles, honoring the literal sweat and tears they pour into building modern society.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Palam tarāda maratte vettakūdadunnu tayi sonnā. 'Nammukku palam ille, ānā āyiram kuruvikku adu dān vīdu.' Namma kidaikkāda onnu mattavangulukku vālve taranum.
stories_or_proverbs.english: The mother said not to cut the tree that gives no fruit. 'We have no fruit, but it is home to a thousand birds.' What we do not get, should give life to others.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: பழம் தராத மரத்தை வெட்டக்கூடாதுன்னு தாய் சொன்னா. 'நமக்கு பழம் இல்லை, ஆனா ஆயிரம் குருவிக்கு அது தான் வீடு.' நமக்கு கிடைக்காத ஒன்னு மத்தவங்களுக்கு வாழ்வை தரணும். (Pazham tharaatha marathai vettakkoodaathunnu thaai sonnaa. 'Namakku pazham illai, aanaa aayiram kuruvikku athu thaan veedu.' Namakku kidaikkaatha onnu mathavangalukku vaazhvai tharanum.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: माँ ने कहा कि फल न देने वाले पेड़ को नहीं काटना चाहिए। 'हमें फल नहीं मिलेगा, लेकिन वह हज़ार पक्षियों का घर है।' जो हमें न मिले, वह दूसरों को जीवन दे। (Maa ne kaha ki phal na dene wale ped ko nahi kaatna chahiye. 'Hamein phal nahi milega, lekin vah hazar pakshiyon ka ghar hai.' Jo hamein na mile, vah dusron ko jeevan de.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: పండు ఇవ్వని చెట్టును నరకకూడదని తల్లి చెప్పింది. 'మనకు పండు లేదు, కానీ వెయ్యి పక్షులకు అదే ఇల్లు.' మనకు దొరకనిది ఇతరులకు జీవితాన్ని ఇవ్వాలి. (Pandu ivvani chettunu narakakudadani talli cheppindi. 'Manaku pandu ledu, kaani veyyi pakshulaku ade illu.' Manaku dorakanidi itarulaku jeevitanni ivvali.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: A testament to the Irula tribe's deep ecological consciousness. Even when struggling for resources, they prioritize the survival of the forest ecosystem and its voiceless creatures over their own immediate needs.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Ūrukkē sōru pōtta vākkattu, innekku verumkāyā irukku. Tāttā tanni illāda nilattilu kokkarai vāsichār. 'Male varalēnnālum, namma pāttu nikkakūdādu.' Nambikke dān namma kadeisi mūchu.
stories_or_proverbs.english: The field that fed the whole village is empty today. The grandfather played the Kokkarai on the dry land. 'Even if the rain doesn't come, our song should not stop.' Hope is our last breath.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: ஊருக்கே சோறு போட்ட வயக்காடு, இன்னைக்கு வெறுங்காயா இருக்கு. தாத்தா தண்ணி இல்லாத நிலத்தில் கொக்கரை வாசித்தார். 'மழை வரலேன்னாலும், நம்ம பாட்டு நிக்கக்கூடாது.' நம்பிக்கை தான் நம்ம கடைசி மூச்சு. (Oorukke soru potta vayakkaadu, innaikku verungaayaa irukku. Thaathaa thanni illaatha nilathil kokkarai vaasithaar. 'Mazhai varalennalum, namma paattu nikkakkoodaathu.' Nambikkai thaan namma kadaisi moochu.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: जिस खेत ने पूरे गाँव को खाना खिलाया, वह आज खाली है। दादाजी ने सूखी ज़मीन पर कोक्कराई (वाद्ययंत्र) बजाया। 'भले ही बारिश न आए, हमारा गीत नहीं रुकना चाहिए।' उम्मीद ही हमारी आखिरी साँस है। (Jis khet ne poore gaon ko khana khilaya, vah aaj khaali hai. Dadaji ne sookhi zameen par Kokkarai bajaya. 'Bhale hi baarish na aaye, hamara geet nahi rukna chahiye.' Ummeed hi hamari aakhiri saans hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: ఊరంతటికీ అన్నం పెట్టిన పొలం, ఈరోజు ఖాళీగా ఉంది. తాతయ్య ఎండిన నేలపై కొక్కరై (వాయిద్యం) వాయించాడు. 'వర్షం రాకపోయినా, మన పాట ఆగకూడదు.' ఆశే మన చివరి శ్వాస. (Oorantatiki annam pettina polam, iroju khaliga undi. Tatayya endina nelapai Kokkarai vayinchadu. 'Varsham rakapoyina, mana paata aagakudadu.' Aashe mana chivari swasa.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: The 'Kokkarai' is a traditional Irula musical instrument. This story evokes sympathy for how climate change and droughts impact their ancestral lands, while showing their incredible resilience through art.

stories_or_proverbs.irula: Pulla paṭinattukku pōgum pōdu, tayi oru kāttu vārttaiye sollittā. 'Kaṭṭadattulu vālnālum, nī yār-nnu inda mannu unakku ñābagam paduttum.' Namma bāse dān namma unmaiyāna vīdu.
stories_or_proverbs.english: As the child went to the city, the mother taught one forest word. 'Even if you live in buildings, this earth will remind you of who you are.' Our language is our true home.
stories_or_proverbs.tamil: பிள்ளை பட்டணத்துக்கு போகும் போது, தாய் ஒரு காட்டு வார்த்தையை சொல்லித்தந்தாள். 'கட்டடத்தில் வாழ்ந்தாலும், நீ யார்னு இந்த மண் உனக்கு ஞாபகப்படுத்தும்.' நம்ம மொழி தான் நம்ம உண்மையான வீடு. (Pillai pattanathukku pogum pothu, thaai oru kaattu vaarthaiyai sollithanthaal. 'Kattadathil vaazhnthaalum, nee yaarnu intha man unakku gnaabagam paduthum.' Namma mozhi thaan namma unmaiyaana veedu.)
stories_or_proverbs.hindi: जब बच्चा शहर जा रहा था, तो माँ ने उसे जंगल का एक शब्द सिखाया। 'भले ही तुम इमारतों में रहो, लेकिन यह मिट्टी तुम्हें याद दिलाएगी कि तुम कौन हो।' हमारी भाषा ही हमारा असली घर है। (Jab bachcha shahar ja raha tha, toh maa ne use jangal ka ek shabd sikhaya. 'Bhale hi tum imaraton mein raho, lekin yah mitti tumhein yaad dilayegi ki tum kaun ho.' Hamari bhasha hi hamara asli ghar hai.)
stories_or_proverbs.telugu: బిడ్డ పట్టణానికి వెళుతున్నప్పుడు, తల్లి ఒక అడవి పదాన్ని నేర్పింది. 'నువ్వు భవనాల్లో జీవించినా, నువ్వు ఎవరివో ఈ మట్టి నీకు గుర్తు చేస్తుంది.' మన భాషే మన నిజమైన ఇల్లు. (Bidda pattananniki velutunnappudu, talli oka adavi padanni nerpindi. 'Nuvvu bhavanallo jeevinchina, nuvvu evarivo ee matti neeku gurtu chestundi.' Mana bhashe mana nijamaina illu.)
stories_or_proverbs.context_note: A deeply fitting final story reflecting the modern Irula experience. As younger generations move away for work and education, preserving their mother tongue becomes the ultimate way to keep their cultural roots and identity alive.

quizzes.question: What is the Irula word for 'Water'?
quizzes.explanation: In Irula, 'tanni' means water. 'sōru' is food/rice, 'neruppu' is fire, and 'pālu' is milk.

quizzes.question: If someone asks you 'Nī epdi irukkiri?', what are they asking?
quizzes.explanation: 'Nī epdi irukkiri?' translates directly to 'How are you?'.

quizzes.question: Which of the following means 'Mother' in Irula?
quizzes.explanation: 'tayi' means mother. 'appa' is father, 'tāttā' is grandfather, and 'pātti' is grandmother.

quizzes.question: What does the command 'Ikke vā' mean?
quizzes.explanation: 'Ikke' means here, and 'vā' is the verb for come. 'Go there' would be 'Akke pō'.

quizzes.question: What color is 'karuppu'?
quizzes.explanation: 'karuppu' is black. White is 'velle', red is 'seveppu', and green is 'pacha'.

quizzes.question: Which of these words means 'Tree'?
quizzes.explanation: 'maram' means tree. 'kādu' is forest, 'male' is mountain, and 'mannu' is soil.

quizzes.question: How do you say 'I am hungry' in Irula?
quizzes.explanation: 'pasi' means hunger. 'vāyaru valikkudu' means stomach pain, and 'tūkkam varudu' means feeling sleepy.

quizzes.question: Which of the following is a number in Irula?
quizzes.explanation: 'onnu' is the number one. 'vīdu' is house, 'mēle' is up, and 'rāttiri' is night.

quizzes.question: Identify the animal: 'pāmbu'.
quizzes.explanation: 'pāmbu' means snake. Dog is 'nāy', elephant is 'yāne', and bird is 'kuruvi'.

quizzes.question: Which pronoun means 'We'?
quizzes.explanation: 'nāmbu' means we. 'nānu' is I, 'nī' is you, and 'avanga' is they.

quizzes.question: What is the Irula word for 'Head'?
quizzes.explanation: 'tale' means head. 'kannu' is eye, 'kālu' is leg, and 'vāy' is mouth.

quizzes.question: Which of these words means 'House' or 'Home'?
quizzes.explanation: 'vīdu' means house. 'kadavu' is door, 'pūṭṭu' is lock, and 'kattil' is cot/bed.

quizzes.question: If an Irula speaker says they are feeling 'santhōsam', how do they feel?
quizzes.explanation: 'santhōsam' means happy/happiness. Sad is 'kavale', angry is 'kōvam', and scared is 'bhayam'.

quizzes.question: If someone points to their 'kayi', what are they pointing at?
quizzes.explanation: 'kayi' is the hand. Stomach is 'vāyaru', tooth is 'pallu', and hair is 'mudi'.

quizzes.question: What is the Irula word for 'Knife'?
quizzes.explanation: 'katti' is a knife. 'kōdāri' is an axe, 'arivālu' is a sickle, and 'veragu' is firewood.

quizzes.question: How do you say 'Pain' in Irula?
quizzes.explanation: 'vali' means pain. 'pasi' is hunger, 'dāgam' is thirst, and 'asadi' is tiredness.

quizzes.question: Which object would you use to sweep the floor?
quizzes.explanation: 'todappam' is a broom. 'pāne' is a pot, 'velakku' is a lamp, and 'sāvi' is a key.

quizzes.question: What emotion does the word 'kōvam' represent?
quizzes.explanation: 'kōvam' means anger. Love is 'pāsam', fear is 'bhayam', and sleepiness is 'tūkkam'.

quizzes.question: What does 'kādu' mean when talking about body parts?
quizzes.explanation: 'kādu' means ear. (Note: 'kādu' also means forest depending on context, but as a body part, it is the ear). Nose is 'mūkku', eye is 'kannu'.

quizzes.question: If you are going to the market, which of these refers to 'Money'?
quizzes.explanation: 'kāsu' means money. 'payi' is bag, 'peṭṭi' is box, and 'tuṇi' is cloth.

quizzes.question: What is the Irula word for 'Milk'?
quizzes.explanation: 'pālu' means milk. 'sōru' is cooked rice/food, 'kari' is meat, and 'mīnu' is fish.

quizzes.question: What does the verb 'tūngu' mean?
quizzes.explanation: 'tūngu' means sleep. Eat is 'tinnu', drink is 'kudi', and walk is 'nada'.

quizzes.question: If a bird is flying 'mēle', where is it?
quizzes.explanation: 'mēle' means up or above. Down is 'kīle', front is 'munnādi', and back is 'pinnādi'.

quizzes.question: How do you say 'Tomorrow' in Irula?
quizzes.explanation: 'nālekki' means tomorrow. 'innekki' is today, 'nēttu' is yesterday, and 'ippo' is now.

quizzes.question: What does the question word 'yāru' mean?
quizzes.explanation: 'yāru' means who. What is 'enna', where is 'ekke', and when is 'eppo'.

quizzes.question: Which of these words means 'Egg'?
quizzes.explanation: 'mutte' is an egg. 'uppu' is salt, 'inippu' is sweet, and 'tēnu' is honey.

quizzes.question: If someone tells you to 'pāru', what are they telling you to do?
quizzes.explanation: 'pāru' means to see or look. Speak is 'pēsu', listen is 'kēlu', and sit is 'ukkāru'.

quizzes.question: How do you tell someone to go 'Straight' in Irula?
quizzes.explanation: 'nēra' means straight. 'valadu' is right, 'edadu' is left, and 'naduvu' is the middle.

quizzes.question: Which word would you use to ask 'How much?' at a market?
quizzes.explanation: 'evvalavu' means how much. 'etene' means how many, 'ēn' is why, and 'epdi' is how.

quizzes.question: What part of the day is 'kāle'?
quizzes.explanation: 'kāle' means morning. Day is 'pagal', evening is 'sāyandaram', and night is 'rāttiri'.

quizzes.question: What is the Irula word for 'Big'?
quizzes.explanation: 'perusu' means big. 'sinnasu' is small, 'pudusu' is new, and 'palasu' is old.

quizzes.question: Which of these words means 'Rain'?
quizzes.explanation: 'male' means rain. 'veyyil' is sunlight, 'kāttu' is wind, and 'mēgam' is cloud.

quizzes.question: Identify the animal: 'puli'.
quizzes.explanation: 'puli' means tiger. Dog is 'nāy', monkey is 'korangu', and elephant is 'yāne'.

quizzes.question: If you ask a shopkeeper 'Idu evvalavu?', what are you asking?
quizzes.explanation: 'Idu evvalavu?' means 'How much is this?'. 'evvalavu' is the question word for 'how much'.

quizzes.question: What is a 'velakku'?
quizzes.explanation: 'velakku' is a lamp or light. Box is 'peṭṭi', broom is 'todappam', and mat is 'pāy'.

quizzes.question: How do you say 'Good' in Irula?
quizzes.explanation: 'nalladu' means good. 'keṭṭadu' means bad, 'sūdu' is hot, and 'kuliru' is cold.

quizzes.question: What does the word 'vēle' mean?
quizzes.explanation: 'vēle' means work or job. Story is 'kade', dream is 'kanavu', and life is 'vālkkai'.

quizzes.question: Which word is used to say 'Always'?
quizzes.explanation: 'eppavum' means always. 'kandippā' is definitely, 'oruvēle' is maybe, and 'mattum' is only.

quizzes.question: What is the Irula word for 'Wind' or 'Air'?
quizzes.explanation: 'kāttu' means wind or air. 'poge' is smoke, 'velicham' is light, and 'neruppu' is fire.

quizzes.question: If someone calls you their 'tolan', who are you to them?
quizzes.explanation: 'tolan' means friend. Enemy is 'ediri', teacher is 'vāttiyār', and farmer is 'vivasāyi'.

quizzes.question: Which of these words means 'Because' in Irula?
quizzes.explanation: 'ēn-nā' means because. 'ānā' is but, 'kūda' is with, and 'appuram' is then/after.

quizzes.question: What is the Irula word for 'Truth'?
quizzes.explanation: 'unme' means truth. 'poy' is lie, 'ragasiyam' is secret, and 'kanavu' is dream.

quizzes.question: How would you ask someone to 'Help me'?
quizzes.explanation: 'Emukku udavi panni.' means 'Help me'. 'Vēgamā ōdu' is run fast, 'Onnum āgale' is nothing happened, and 'Enna āchu?' is what happened.

quizzes.question: If something is 'romba' hot, what does 'romba' mean?
quizzes.explanation: 'romba' means very or much. A little is 'konjam', slowly is 'mella', and nothing is 'onnumille'.

quizzes.question: What does the word 'vāsane' refer to?
quizzes.explanation: 'vāsane' is smell or fragrance. Sound is 'sattam', taste is 'rusi', and light is 'velicham'.

quizzes.question: What are you asking someone to do if you say 'Konjam iru'?
quizzes.explanation: 'Konjam iru' means wait a little. Come now is 'Ippo vā', speak slowly is 'Mella pēsu', and forgive me is 'Emme mannichidu'.

quizzes.question: Which verb means to 'Read' or 'Study'?
quizzes.explanation: 'padi' means to read or study. 'pāru' is to see, 'sollu' is to tell, and 'kadi' is to bite.

quizzes.question: What is the Irula word for a 'Child'?
quizzes.explanation: 'pulla' means child. 'payan' is boy, 'ponnu' is girl, and 'ālu' is person.

quizzes.question: How do you say 'Week' in Irula?
quizzes.explanation: 'vāram' means week. 'nālu' is day, 'māsam' is month, and 'varusam' is year.

quizzes.question: Translate the concept 'olagam':
quizzes.explanation: 'olagam' means world. Life is 'vālkkai', God is 'sāmi', and help is 'udavi'.

lines.hindi: यह बहुत ज़्यादा है। थोड़ा कम करो। (Yah bahut zyada hai. Thoda kam karo.)
lines.telugu: ఇది చాలా ఎక్కువ. కొంచెం తగ్గించు. (Idi chaala ekkuva. Konchem tagginchu.)

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.hindi: ठीक है, इसे लो। (Theek hai, ise lo.)

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.hindi: क्या तुम्हारे पास छुट्टे हैं? (Kya tumhare paas chhutte hain?)
lines.telugu: నీ దగ్గర చిల్లర ఉందా? (Nee daggara chillara unda?)

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.hindi: हाँ, मेरे पास हैं। (Haan, mere paas hain.)
lines.telugu: అవును, నా దగ్గర ఉంది. (Avunu, naa daggara undi.)

lines.speaker: Traveler
lines.hindi: जंगल कहाँ है? (Jangal kahan hai?)

lines.speaker: Local
lines.hindi: सीधे जाओ। (Seedhe jao.)

lines.speaker: Traveler
lines.hindi: क्या यह दूर है? (Kya yah door hai?)

lines.speaker: Local
lines.tamil: இல்ல, அது கிட்டே இருக்கு. (Illa, athu kittae irukku.)
lines.hindi: नहीं, यह पास है। (Nahi, yah paas hai.)
lines.telugu: లేదు, అది దగ్గరగా ఉంది. (Ledu, adi daggaraga undi.)

lines.speaker: Traveler
lines.hindi: बहुत खुशी हुई / धन्यवाद। (Bahut khushi hui / Dhanyawad.)

lines.speaker: Host
lines.hindi: अंदर आओ, बैठो। (Andar aao, baitho.)

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.hindi: मुझे थकान हो रही है। (Mujhe thakan ho rahi hai.)

lines.speaker: Host
lines.tamil: உனக்கு பசி எடுக்குதா? தண்ணீர் குடி. (Unakku pasi edukkuthaa? Thanneer kudi.)
lines.hindi: क्या तुम्हें भूख लग रही है? पानी पियो। (Kya tumhein bhookh lag rahi hai? Paani piyo.)
lines.telugu: నీకు ఆకలి వేస్తోందా? నీళ్లు తాగు. (Neeku aakali vestondaa? Neellu taagu.)

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.tamil: ஆமா, எனக்கு கொஞ்சம் சோறு கொடு. (Aama, enakku konjam soru kodu.)
lines.hindi: हाँ, मुझे थोड़ा खाना दो। (Haan, mujhe thoda khaana do.)
lines.telugu: అవును, నాకు కొంచెం అన్నం ఇవ్వు. (Avunu, naaku konchem annam ivvu.)

lines.speaker: Host
lines.hindi: अच्छे से खाओ। (Achchhe se khao.)

lines.speaker: Healer
lines.hindi: क्या हुआ? (Kya hua?)

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.hindi: मेरे पैर में दर्द है। (Mere pair mein dard hai.)
lines.telugu: నాకు కాలు నొప్పిగా ఉంది. (Naaku kaalu noppiga undi.)

lines.speaker: Healer
lines.english: Don't be scared. Take this medicine.
lines.tamil: பயப்படாதே. இந்த மருந்து எடு. (Bhayappadaathae. Intha marunthu edu.)
lines.hindi: डरो मत। यह दवा लो। (Daro mat. Yah dawa lo.)
lines.telugu: భయపడవద్దు. ఈ మందు తీసుకో. (Bhayapadavaddu. Ee mandu teesuko.)

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.hindi: इसे कब खाना है? (Ise kab khaana hai?)

lines.speaker: Healer
lines.english: Eat it in the morning and night.
lines.hindi: इसे सुबह और रात को खाओ। (Ise subah aur raat ko khao.)
lines.telugu: ఉదయం మరియు రాత్రి తిను. (Udayam mariyu raatri tinu.)

lines.speaker: Person A
lines.tamil: நீ என்ன வேலை பண்ணுகிறாய்? (Nee enna velai pannugiraai?)
lines.hindi: तुम क्या काम कर रहे हो? (Tum kya kaam kar rahe ho?)
lines.telugu: నువ్వు ఏం పని చేస్తున్నావు? (Nuvvu em pani chestunnavu?)

lines.speaker: Person B
lines.hindi: मैं लकड़ियाँ इकट्ठा कर रहा हूँ। (Main lakdiyan ikattha kar raha hoon.)

lines.speaker: Person A
lines.hindi: ध्यान से, धीरे जाओ। (Dhyan se, dheere jao.)

lines.speaker: Person B
lines.hindi: ठीक है, मैं ध्यान रखूँगा। (Theek hai, main dhyan rakhunga.)

lines.speaker: Person A
lines.hindi: आज बहुत गर्मी है। (Aaj bahut garmi hai.)
lines.telugu: ఈ రోజు చాలా వేడిగా ఉంది. (Ee roju chaala vediga undi.)

lines.speaker: Person B
lines.hindi: हाँ, धूप बहुत तेज़ है। (Haan, dhoop bahut tez hai.)
lines.telugu: అవును, ఎండ ఎక్కువగా ఉంది. (Avunu, enda ekkuvaga undi.)

lines.speaker: Person A
lines.hindi: क्या बारिश होगी? (Kya baarish hogi?)

lines.speaker: Person B
lines.english: Maybe it will come at night.
lines.hindi: शायद रात को आ सकती है। (Shayad raat ko aa sakti hai.)

lines.speaker: Person A
lines.hindi: संभलकर चलो! (Sambhalkar chalo!)

lines.speaker: Person B
lines.hindi: क्यों? क्या हुआ? (Kyon? Kya hua?)

lines.speaker: Person A
lines.tamil: அங்கே ஒரு பாம்பு இருக்கு. (Ange oru paambu irukku.)
lines.hindi: वहाँ एक सांप है। (Wahan ek saanp hai.)
lines.telugu: అక్కడ ఒక పాము ఉంది. (Akkada oka paamu undi.)

lines.speaker: Person B
lines.hindi: अरे! तेज़ भागो! (Are! Tez bhago!)

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.hindi: तुम क्यों रो रहे हो? (Tum kyon ro rahe ho?)

lines.speaker: Child
lines.hindi: मुझे भूख लग रही है। (Mujhe bhookh lag rahi hai.)

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.hindi: रो मत। दूध पियो। (Ro mat. Doodh piyo.)

lines.speaker: Child
lines.hindi: धन्यवाद, माँ। (Dhanyawad, maa.)

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.irula: Ippo rāttiri āchu. Nānu pōgitu varugēnu.
lines.english: Now it is night. I am taking leave.
lines.tamil: இப்போ ராத்திரி ஆச்சு. நான் போயிட்டு வரேன். (Ippo raathiri aachu. Naan poittu varen.)
lines.hindi: अब रात हो गई है। मैं चलता हूँ। (Ab raat ho gayi hai. Main chalta hoon.)
lines.telugu: ఇప్పుడు రాత్రి అయింది. నేను వెళ్లి వస్తాను. (Ippudu raatri ayindi. Nenu velli vastanu.)

lines.speaker: Host
lines.hindi: ठीक है, धीरे जाना। (Theek hai, dheere jaana.)

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.hindi: कल सुबह आना। (Kal subah aana.)

lines.speaker: Host
lines.hindi: ज़रूर आऊँगा। (Zaroor aaunga.)

riddle.irula: Udalukku teriyum, kannukku teriyādu. Adu enna?
riddle.english: The body can feel it, but the eyes cannot see it. What is it?
riddle.tamil: உடலுக்கு தெரியும், கண்ணுக்கு தெரியாது. அது என்ன? (Udalukku theriyum, kannukku theriyaathu. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: शरीर को महसूस होता है, पर आँखों को नहीं दिखता। यह क्या है? (Shareer ko mahsoos hota hai, par aankhon ko nahi dikhta. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: శరీరానికి తెలుస్తుంది, కానీ కళ్ళకు కనిపించదు. అది ఏమిటి? (Shareeraniki telustundi, kaani kallaku kanipinchadu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Pagalil kūda varum, rāttiriyil kāṇāma pōgum. Adu enna?
riddle.english: It comes with you in the day, but disappears at night. What is it?
riddle.tamil: பகலில் கூட வரும், ராத்திரியில் காணாமல் போகும். அது என்ன? (Pagalil kooda varum, raathiriyil kaanaamal pogum. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: दिन में साथ आता है, रात में गायब हो जाता है। यह क्या है? (Din mein saath aata hai, raat mein gayab ho jata hai. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: పగలు తోడుగా వస్తుంది, రాత్రి మాయమైపోతుంది. అది ఏమిటి? (Pagalu toduga vastundi, raatri maayamaipotundi. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Tanni kudippātti satturuvān, kāttu adittāl perusāvān. Adu enna?
riddle.english: If given water it dies, if wind blows it grows big. What is it?
riddle.tamil: தண்ணீர் குடித்தால் செத்துருவான், காற்று அடித்தால் பெருசாவான். அது என்ன? (Thanneer kudithaal sethuruvaan, kaatru adithaal perusaavaan. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: पानी पीने से मर जाता है, हवा चलने से बड़ा हो जाता है। यह क्या है? (Paani peene se mar jata hai, hawa chalne se bada ho jata hai. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: నీరు త్రాగితే చనిపోతాడు, గాలి వీస్తే పెద్దవాడవుతాడు. అది ఏమిటి? (Neeru traagite chanipotaadu, gaali veeste peddavaadavutaadu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Oru osaramāna marattil, orē oru palam. Adu enna?
riddle.english: On a very tall tree, there is only one fruit. What is it?
riddle.tamil: ஒரு உயரமான மரத்தில், ஒரே ஒரு பழம். அது என்ன? (Oru uyaramaana marathil, ore oru pazham. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: एक बहुत ऊँचे पेड़ पर, बस एक ही फल। यह क्या है? (Ek bahut oonche ped par, bas ek hi phal. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: ఒక ఎత్తైన చెట్టు మీద, ఒకే ఒక పండు. అది ఏమిటి? (Oka ettaina chettu meeda, oke oka pandu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Vānatil pūkkum pūvukku ennave mudiyādu. Adu enna?
riddle.english: The flowers that bloom in the sky cannot be counted. What are they?
riddle.tamil: வானத்தில் பூக்கும் பூவுக்கு எண்ணவே முடியாது. அது என்ன? (Vaanathil pookkum poovukku ennave mudiyaathu. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: आसमान में खिलने वाले फूलों को गिना नहीं जा सकता। वे क्या हैं? (Aasman mein khilne wale phoolon ko gina nahi ja sakta. Ve kya hain?)
riddle.telugu: ఆకాశంలో వికసించే పూలను లెక్కించలేము. అవి ఏమిటి? (Aakasamlo vikasinche poolanu lekkinchalemu. Avi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Velle vīṭṭukku kadavu ille. Adu enna?
riddle.english: The white house has no door. What is it?
riddle.tamil: வெள்ளை வீட்டுக்கு கதவு இல்லை. அது என்ன? (Vellai veettukku kathavu illai. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: सफेद घर का कोई दरवाज़ा नहीं है। यह क्या है? (Safed ghar ka koi darwaza nahi hai. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: తెల్లని ఇంటికి తలుపు లేదు. అది ఏమిటి? (Tellani intiki talupu ledu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Mēle pacha, ullukka velle, naduvil tanni. Adu enna?
riddle.english: Green outside, white inside, water in the middle. What is it?
riddle.tamil: மேலே பச்சை, உள்ளே வெள்ளை, நடுவில் தண்ணீர். அது என்ன? (Maele pachai, ulle vellai, naduvil thanneer. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: बाहर हरा, अंदर सफेद, बीच में पानी। यह क्या है? (Bahar hara, andar safed, beech mein paani. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: పైన ఆకుపచ్చ, లోపల తెలుపు, మధ్యలో నీరు. అది ఏమిటి? (Paina aakupachcha, lopala telupu, madhyalo neeru. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Pagal ellām nadappān, rāttiri ellām tūnguvān, vāy illāda ālu. Adu yāru?
riddle.english: Walks all day, sleeps all night, a person with no mouth. Who is it?
riddle.tamil: பகல் எல்லாம் நடப்பான், ராத்திரி எல்லாம் தூங்குவான், வாய் இல்லாத ஆள். அது யார்? (Pagal ellaam nadappaan, raathiri ellaam thoonguvaan, vaay illaatha aal. Athu yaar?)
riddle.hindi: दिन भर चलता है, रात भर सोता है, बिना मुँह का इंसान। यह क्या है? (Din bhar chalta hai, raat bhar sota hai, bina munh ka insaan. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: పగలంతా నడుస్తాడు, రాత్రంతా నిద్రపోతాడు, నోరు లేని మనిషి. ఎవరు? (Pagalanta nadustaadu, raatrantaa nidrapotaadu, noru leni manishi. Evaru?)

riddle.irula: Siveppu gugaikkul muppadu velle kallu. Adu enna?
riddle.english: Inside a red cave, thirty white stones. What is it?
riddle.tamil: சிவப்பு குகைக்குள் முப்பது வெள்ளை கல்லு. அது என்ன? (Sivappu kugaikkul muppathu vellai kallu. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: लाल गुफा के अंदर तीस सफेद पत्थर। यह क्या है? (Laal gufa ke andar tees safed patthar. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: ఎర్రటి గుహలో ముప్పై తెల్లటి రాళ్ళు. అది ఏమిటి? (Errati guhalo muppai tellati raallu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Nī pāttā, aduvum pākkum. Nī sirittā, aduvum sirikkum. Adu enna?
riddle.english: If you look, it also looks. If you laugh, it also laughs. What is it?
riddle.tamil: நீ பார்த்தால், அதுவும் பார்க்கும். நீ சிரித்தால், அதுவும் சிரிக்கும். அது என்ன? (Nee paarthaal, athuvum paarkkum. Nee sirithaal, athuvum sirikkum. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: तुम देखो तो वो भी देखे, तुम हँसो तो वो भी हँसे। यह क्या है? (Tum dekho to vo bhi dekhe, tum hanso to vo bhi hanse. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: నువ్వు చూస్తే అది చూస్తుంది. నువ్వు నవ్వితే అది నవ్వుతుంది. అది ఏమిటి? (Nuvvu chooste adi choostundi. Nuvvu navvite adi navvutundi. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Kannu irukku, ānā pākkamudiyādu. Adu enna?
riddle.english: It has an eye, but it cannot see. What is it?
riddle.tamil: கண் இருக்கு, ஆனா பார்க்க முடியாது. அது என்ன? (Kan irukku, aanaa paarkka mudiyaathu. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: आँख है पर देख नहीं सकती। यह क्या है? (Aankh hai par dekh nahi sakti. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: కన్ను ఉంది కానీ చూడలేదు. అది ఏమిటి? (Kannu undi kaani choodaledu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Rāttiri vānatil velli taṭṭu, ānā sōru tinna mudiyādu. Adu enna?
riddle.english: A silver plate in the night sky, but you cannot eat food from it. What is it?
riddle.tamil: ராத்திரி வானத்தில் வெள்ளி தட்டு, ஆனா சோறு தின்ன முடியாது. அது என்ன? (Raathiri vaanathil velli thattu, aanaa soru thinna mudiyaathu. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: रात के आसमान में चाँदी की थाली, पर उसमें खा नहीं सकते। यह क्या है? (Raat ke aasman mein chaandi ki thaali, par usmein khaa nahi sakte. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: రాత్రి ఆకాశంలో వెండి పళ్ళెం, కానీ అన్నం తినలేము. అది ఏమిటి? (Raatri aakasamlo vendi pallem, kaani annam tinalemu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Sinna kāvālkāran, vāyaru perusu, sāvi pōttā torakkum. Adu enna?
riddle.english: A small guard with a big stomach, it opens when you put the key in. What is it?
riddle.tamil: சின்ன காவல்காரன், வயிறு பெரிசு, சாவி போட்டால் திறக்கும். அது என்ன? (Sinna kaavalkaaran, vayiru perisu, saavi pottaal thirakkum. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: छोटा सा चौकीदार, पेट बड़ा, चाबी लगाने पर खुलता है। यह क्या है? (Chhota sa chaukidaar, pet bada, chaabi lagane par khulta hai. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: చిన్న కాపలాదారుడు, పొట్ట పెద్దది, తాళం వేస్తే తెరుచుకుంటుంది. అది ఏమిటి? (Chinna kaapalaadaarudu, potta peddadi, taalam veste teruchukuntundi. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Mēleyum pōgum, kīleyum pōgum, ānā nagarādu. Adu enna?
riddle.english: It goes up, and it goes down, but it never moves. What is it?
riddle.tamil: மேலேயும் போகும், கீழேயும் போகும், ஆனா நகராது. அது என்ன? (Maeleyum pogum, keezheyum pogum, aanaa nagaraathu. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: ऊपर भी जाए, नीचे भी जाए, पर अपनी जगह से न हिले। यह क्या है? (Upar bhi jaye, neeche bhi jaye, par apni jagah se na hile. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: పైకి వెళుతుంది, కిందకి వెళుతుంది, కానీ కదలదు. అది ఏమిటి? (Paiki velutundi, kindaki velutundi, kaani kadaladu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Vīdu ellām suttam pannum, ānā mūleyil nikkum. Adu enna?
riddle.english: It cleans the whole house, but stands in the corner. What is it?
riddle.tamil: வீடு எல்லாம் சுத்தம் பண்ணும், ஆனா மூலையில் நிற்கும். அது என்ன? (Veedu ellaam suttham pannum, aanaa moolaiyil nirkkum. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: पूरे घर को साफ करे, पर कोने में खड़ी रहे। यह क्या है? (Poore ghar ko saaf kare, par kone mein khadi rahe. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: ఇల్లంతా శుభ్రం చేస్తుంది, కానీ మూలలో నిలబడుతుంది. అది ఏమిటి? (Illanta subhram chestundi, kaani moolalo nilabadutundi. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Sirusā irukkumpōdu surundu irukkum, torandā sōru tinnuvōmu. Adu enna?
riddle.english: When young it is rolled up, when open we eat food on it. What is it?
riddle.tamil: சிறுசா இருக்கும்போது சுருண்டு இருக்கும், திறந்தா சோறு தின்னுவோம். அது என்ன? (Sirusaa irukkumbothu surundu irukkum, thiranthaa soru thinnuvom. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: जब छोटा हो तो मुड़ा हुआ, खुलने पर हम उस पर खाते हैं। यह क्या है? (Jab chhota ho to muda hua, khulne par hum us par khaate hain. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: చిన్నగా ఉన్నప్పుడు చుట్టుకుని ఉంటుంది, తెరిచాక అన్నం తింటాము. అది ఏమిటి? (Chinnaga unnappudu chuttukuni untundi, terichaaka annam tintaamu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Tanni-il nīndum, ānā padagu ille. Adu enna?
riddle.english: It swims in water, but it is not a boat. What is it?
riddle.tamil: தண்ணியில் நீந்தும், ஆனா படகு இல்லை. அது என்ன? (Thanniyil neenthum, aanaa padagu illai. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: पानी में तैरती है, पर नाव नहीं। यह क्या है? (Paani mein tairti hai, par naav nahi. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: నీటిలో ఈదుతుంది, కానీ పడవ కాదు. అది ఏమిటి? (Neetilo eedutundi, kaani padava kaadu. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Dinamum vettinālum, tirumbavum valarum. Adu enna?
riddle.english: Even if you cut it every day, it will grow again. What is it?
riddle.tamil: தினமும் வெட்டினாலும், திரும்பவும் வளரும். அது என்ன? (Dhinamum vettinaalum, thirumbavum valarum. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: रोज़ काटो, फिर भी बढ़ता रहे। यह क्या है? (Roz kaato, phir bhi badhta rahe. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: ప్రతిరోజూ కత్తిరించినా, మళ్ళీ పెరుగుతుంది. అది ఏమిటి? (Pratiroju kattirinchina, malli perugutundi. Adi emiti?)

riddle.irula: Kannu mūdi, vēra olagattukku konda pōgum. Adu enna?
riddle.english: It closes your eyes and takes you to another world. What is it?
riddle.tamil: கண்ணை மூடி, வேற உலகத்துக்கு கொண்டு போகும். அது என்ன? (Kannai moodi, vera ulagathukku kondu pogum. Athu enna?)
riddle.hindi: आँखें बंद कर, दूसरी दुनिया में ले जाए। यह क्या है? (Aankhein band kar, doosri duniya mein le jaye. Yah kya hai?)
riddle.telugu: కళ్ళు మూసి, వేరే ప్రపంచానికి తీసుకువెళుతుంది. అది ఏమిటి? (Kallu moosi, vere prapanchaniki teesukuvelutundi. Adi emiti?)

grammar_rules.explanation: To make a noun plural in Irula, we typically add the suffix '-ga' or '-nga' to the end of the root word, similar to spoken Tamil.
The basic form of an action verb (like 'vā' or 'pō') is used to command one person informally. To make it respectful or plural, add '-nga' to the end.
When speaking about an action you are currently doing ('I am...'), attach the suffix '-gēnu' or '-girēnu' to the verb root.

examples.hindi: मैं जा रहा हूँ। (Main ja raha hoon.)
मैं खा रहा हूँ। (Main kha raha hoon.)

grammar_rules.explanation: To talk about actions you completed in the past ('I did...'), verbs take past-tense suffixes like '-tēnu', '-ndēnu', or '-nēnu'.
To turn a statement into a Yes/No question in Irula, simply add a long '-ā' sound to the very last word of the sentence.

examples.english: Is this good? (from 'Idu nalladu' = This is good)
examples.hindi: क्या यह अच्छा है? (Kya yah achchha hai?)

examples.english: Is rain coming? (from 'Male varudu' = Rain is coming)
examples.hindi: क्या बारिश आ रही है? (Kya baarish aa rahi hai?)

grammar_rules.explanation: To tell someone NOT to do an action, add the suffix '-āde' to the root verb.
To show ownership, the pronouns 'nānu' (I) and 'nī' (you) change into 'en' (my) and 'un' (your) before a noun.
To say you are going TO a destination, attach the suffix '-kku' or '-ukku' to the noun (similar to the Dative case in other Dravidian languages).

examples.hindi: घर -> घर को / घर की ओर (Ghar -> Ghar ko)

grammar_rules.explanation: To say something is located IN or AT a specific place, attach the locative suffix '-le' to the noun.
To talk about actions you will do in the future, verbs take suffixes like '-vēnu' or '-pēnu' for the first person ('I').
